theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What does "human relations" mean at work?
options: Only the rules written in the staff handbook
The pay and holidays each worker is given
How people get along and work with each other
The machines and tools that a business owns and uses

questions.stem: Why are good human relations important in a workplace?
options: They help people work well together and serve customers
They mean that nobody ever needs to follow the rules
They stop the business from ever needing a supervisor
They make sure that every worker gets the same pay rise

questions.stem: What is a "positive attitude" at work?
options: Agreeing with everything just so that you avoid trouble
Smiling only when the supervisor is watching
Doing only the jobs that you enjoy doing most
Looking for solutions and being willing to help

questions.stem: Which of these best describes "self-awareness"?
options: Knowing what everyone else thinks of your work
Knowing your own strengths, weaknesses and moods
Checking how you look in the mirror before work each day
Being aware of every rule in the building

questions.stem: A co-worker is having a bad day and snaps at you. What is the best way to respond?
options: Snap back so they know how it feels to be spoken to like that
Stay calm and ask later, in private, if they are all right
Tell all the other workers about it at lunch time
Refuse to work with that person ever again

questions.stem: You feel very angry with a customer. What should you do first?
options: Tell the customer exactly what you think of them
Walk out of the building and go home for the day
Raise your voice so that the customer will listen
Take a slow breath and keep your voice calm

questions.stem: What is "empathy"?
options: Understanding how another person feels
Feeling sorry for yourself when things go wrong
Agreeing with whatever the customer says
Doing a job faster than everyone else

questions.stem: A new co-worker comes from a different parish and has a different religion. How should you treat them?
options: Avoid them until they learn to fit in with you
Make jokes about their beliefs to break the ice
With the same respect and fairness as anyone else
Only speak to them when the supervisor tells you to

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of respecting diversity at work?
options: Treating people fairly whatever their age, sex or background
Giving the best jobs only to friends from your own district
Laughing along when others joke about a person's disability
Only hiring people who look and think the same as you do

questions.stem: A co-worker keeps making unwanted comments about how a trainee looks. What is this?
options: Friendly workplace humour
Normal customer service
Harassment
Team building

questions.stem: What should you do if you are being bullied at work?
options: Keep quiet and hope that it will stop by itself
Keep a record and report it to a supervisor
Bully the person back so that they leave you alone
Leave the job without telling anyone the reason

questions.stem: What is a "team" at work?
options: A list of every worker who gets paid at the end of each week
A group of friends who meet after work hours
The managers who own and run the business
A group of people working together towards a shared goal

questions.stem: Which behaviour helps a team most?
options: Keeping useful information to yourself
Blaming other members whenever something goes wrong
Doing only your own part and nothing more
Sharing information and helping when needed

questions.stem: A team member, Shanice, finishes her part of the job early. What is the best thing for her to do?
options: Sit on her phone until it is time to go home
Ask the team or supervisor where she can help
Leave early because her own part is finished
Start a new job that nobody has asked for yet

questions.stem: Why should team members agree on who does each task?
options: So that one person can do all of the work alone
So that the job takes much longer than planned
So that work is not missed or done twice
So that the supervisor has nothing at all to do

questions.stem: In a team, what does it mean to be "reliable"?
options: Others can count on you to do what you agreed
You always have the newest phone and tools
You are the loudest voice in every meeting
You can do the work of the whole team by yourself

questions.stem: What is the first step in sorting out a disagreement between two co-workers?
options: Decide straight away who is right and who is wrong
Tell the manager to sack one of the two of them
Let each person explain their side calmly
Ignore it and hope it goes away by itself

questions.stem: Which is the best way to deal with a conflict with a co-worker?
options: Post about the problem on social media that night
Refuse to speak to them again for the whole week
Get other workers to take your side against them
Talk privately and look for a fair solution

questions.stem: What does it mean to "compromise" in a disagreement?
options: One person gets everything they asked for
Each side gives a little to reach an agreement
Both sides stop talking to each other for good
The supervisor decides and nobody can speak

questions.stem: When should a supervisor be asked to help with a conflict?
options: When the people involved cannot sort it out themselves
Before the two people involved have even tried to talk
Every time anyone disagrees about anything at all
Never, because supervisors must not hear about it

questions.stem: Who is an "internal customer"?
options: A person who buys from the business for the first time
A co-worker or another department you provide work for
A supplier who delivers materials to the business
A customer who only ever shops inside the building itself

questions.stem: A client in the salon or a customer at the workshop is waiting. What should you do?
options: Greet them politely and tell them how long they will wait
Carry on chatting to co-workers until they speak first
Pretend you do not see them until you are completely free
Tell them to come back another day when it is quiet

questions.stem: Why is it important to keep the promises you make to customers?
options: So that the business can charge them a lot more
So that customers stop asking you any questions
So that you do not have to talk to them again
So that customers trust you and come back again

questions.stem: A customer thanks you for good work. What is the best reply?
options: Say nothing and walk off to the next job
Tell them it was not good and point out faults
Smile, thank them and say you are glad to help
Ask them for extra money as a tip straight away

questions.stem: Which of these is good workplace manners?
options: Saying please and thank you to co-workers
Using a co-worker's tools without asking
Playing loud music while others work
Arriving late to meetings without a word

questions.stem: You borrow a co-worker's tool or styling brush. What should you do?
options: Keep it until they come and ask for it back
Lend it on to someone else without asking
Leave it wherever you finished using it
Return it clean, on time and in good order

questions.stem: Why should you respect a co-worker's privacy?
options: Because it is the only rule in the handbook
So that you can find out more about them later
It builds trust and shows respect for them
So that nobody ever speaks to anyone at work

questions.stem: What is "constructive criticism"?
options: Criticism that is meant to hurt a person's feelings
Feedback that points out a problem and how to improve
Comments made only about the way a person looks
A complaint made about a co-worker behind their back

questions.stem: How should you accept a correction from your instructor?
options: Argue until the instructor gives up
Sulk and do less work for the rest of the day
Laugh it off and carry on in the same way
Thank them, think about it and try to improve

questions.stem: What is "morale" in a workplace?
options: The rules that all staff must sign
The money the business makes each month
How confident and happy the staff feel
The time that each shift starts and ends

questions.stem: Which of these is most likely to lower team morale?
options: Gossip and unfair treatment
Praise given for a good piece of work
Clear instructions and fair rules
Fair sharing of tasks

questions.stem: How do you build trust with co-workers?
options: By telling them only what they want to hear
By being honest and doing what you say you will
By sharing their secrets with other people
By taking credit for work that others have done

questions.stem: You make a mistake that affects a co-worker's job. What should you do?
options: Hide it and hope that nobody ever finds out
Admit it, say sorry and help to put it right
Blame the mistake on the tools or the materials
Say nothing and let the co-worker take the blame

questions.stem: A customer uses a wheelchair. Which is the most respectful approach?
options: Speak only to the person who came in with them, not to them
Push the wheelchair without asking first
Speak to them directly and ask how you can help
Avoid serving them in case you get it wrong

questions.stem: A young woman joins the welding class, or a young man joins the beauty class. How should the others behave?
options: Tell them that the trade is not meant for them
Give them only the easiest jobs to do
Make jokes so that they feel part of the group
Treat them as an equal member of the class

questions.stem: What does keeping "professional boundaries" with customers mean?
options: Keeping the relationship friendly but about the work
Never speaking to a customer unless they speak first
Sharing your personal problems to seem friendly
Giving your best friends a lower price than others

questions.stem: Which is a healthy way to deal with stress from work relationships?
options: Shouting at the next person who speaks to you at work
Keeping all your feelings bottled up inside
Talking to someone you trust and taking short breaks
Skipping meals so that you get more work done

questions.stem: A visitor from another country greets you in a way you are not used to. What is the best response?
options: Laugh at the greeting and tell your friends about it
Respond politely and respect their custom
Ignore them until they greet you the Jamaican way
Tell them that their greeting is wrong

questions.stem: In a team meeting, a quiet member has not spoken. What can you do?
options: Invite them to share their view
Speak for them without asking
Tell them that quiet people are lazy
Ignore them so the meeting is faster

questions.stem: You do not agree with an instruction from your supervisor, but it is safe and fair. What should you do?
options: Refuse to do it until they change their mind
Do the job badly so that the supervisor sees it is wrong
Complain about the supervisor to the customers
Do it, and share your view politely at a good time

questions.stem: Why is gossip harmful in a workplace?
options: It spreads stories that can hurt people and break trust
It helps people get the facts about a problem quickly
It makes every worker feel more respected and valued
It gives the supervisor clear and useful facts about each worker

questions.stem: Which is a good way to welcome a new member of staff?
options: Leave them alone so that they can learn it by themselves
Introduce yourself and show them where things are
Give them all of the jobs that nobody else wants
Test them with tricks to see if they are tough

questions.stem: What does it mean to be "assertive"?
options: To get your own way by shouting at people
To always give in to others so that there is never an argument
To state your view clearly while respecting others
To refuse to listen to anyone else's view

questions.stem: A co-worker posts a photo of a customer online without asking. Why is this wrong?
options: Photos of customers are only allowed on weekdays
The photo will make the business too popular
Only supervisors are allowed to own phones
It breaks the customer's privacy and trust

questions.stem: On a building job, a welder, an electrician and a cleaner all need the same area. What is the best way to work?
options: Whoever arrives first takes the area for the whole day
Agree a plan together so that each can work safely
Each person works there at once and ignores the others
Wait for the supervisor to send the others home

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What word names the beliefs a person holds about what is right and important, such as honesty and respect?
What is the word for treating a person unfairly because of their race, sex, religion or disability?
What is the word for an unfair opinion formed about a person or group before you know them?
What is the word for a fixed, over-simple idea of what a whole group of people is like?
What one word means people working well together as a team?
What is the word for being able to control your feelings and actions, even when you are upset?
What is the word for being truthful and not stealing, lying or cheating?
What is the word for a disagreement or clash between people at work?
A person from outside the business who pays for its goods or services is called what kind of customer?
What is the name for a neutral person who helps two sides settle a disagreement?
What word describes keeping private information about customers and co-workers secret?
What do we call the polite ways of behaving towards others, such as saying "good morning" and "thank you"?
What word describes being willing to change your plans or methods when things change at work?
What word names the way a person thinks and feels about their work, which shows in how they behave?
What word means staying calm and not getting annoyed when you have to wait or a job takes a long time?

essays.stem: Explain why good human relations matter in a workplace, for the workers, the customers and the business.
essays.modelAnswer: Human relations are the way people at work get along, treat each other and work together. For workers, good relations make the workplace pleasant and safe. People feel respected, help each other, share information and are less stressed, so they are more likely to stay in the job. For customers, good relations mean they are greeted politely, listened to and served well, whether in a salon, a hotel or a welding shop. Customers who feel valued come back and tell others. For the business, good relations mean less conflict, fewer mistakes, less time lost to arguments, and better teamwork, so work is done on time and to a good standard. This builds a good name for the business and helps it earn more and keep its staff.
markingPoints: Says what human relations are
Benefit to workers: respect, help, less stress, staff stay
Benefit to customers: polite, good service, they return
Benefit to the business: fewer mistakes and conflicts, work on time
Good reputation and earnings

essays.stem: Describe the qualities of a good team member. Give an example from a welding shop, a beauty salon or another workplace.
essays.modelAnswer: A good team member is reliable: they arrive on time and do the tasks they agreed to do. They communicate, sharing information and telling others about problems early. They co-operate and are willing to help when someone falls behind, and they do not leave others to do the heavy or dirty jobs. They respect other members, listen to their ideas and do not gossip or blame. They accept feedback and keep learning. They also follow the safety rules, because one person's mistake can hurt the whole team. For example, in a welding shop, Andre finishes cutting his steel early, so he asks the group leader if he can help Kemar grind and clean the joints, and he tells the team when the grinder disc is worn so that it is changed before anyone is hurt.
markingPoints: Reliable and on time; does agreed tasks
Communicates and shares information
Helps others and co-operates
Respects others; no gossip or blame; accepts feedback
A suitable workplace example

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would take to settle a disagreement between yourself and a co-worker.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would stay calm and not argue in front of customers or other workers. I would ask the co-worker to talk at a good time, in a quiet, private place. I would let them explain their side fully without cutting in, and I would listen and show that I understand. Then I would explain my side calmly, using "I" statements such as "I feel rushed when the station is not cleaned" rather than blaming. Together we would look for the real problem and think of a few possible solutions. We would agree a fair solution where each of us may give a little, for example taking turns to clean the shared work area. If we could not agree, I would ask the supervisor to help. Later I would check that the solution is working.
markingPoints: Stays calm and picks a private place and good time
Listens to the other person's side without interrupting
Explains own side calmly without blaming
Looks for solutions and agrees a fair compromise
Asks a supervisor if needed and follows up

essays.stem: Explain what discrimination is, why it is harmful at work, and what a worker should do if they see it happen.
essays.modelAnswer: Discrimination is treating someone unfairly because of who they are, such as their race, colour, sex, age, religion, where they come from, or a disability. Examples are refusing to serve a customer because of their background, giving the worst jobs to a worker because of her sex, or making jokes about someone's disability. It is harmful because the person is hurt, loses confidence and may leave. It breaks trust in the team, lowers morale and can lead to complaints and legal trouble for the business. Customers who see it may stop coming. If a worker sees discrimination, they should not join in or laugh. They should support the person, write down what happened, and report it to a supervisor or manager so that it is dealt with under the workplace's rules.
markingPoints: Defines discrimination as unfair treatment because of who a person is
Gives at least one workplace example
Harm to the person: hurt, loss of confidence
Harm to the team or business: trust, morale, complaints
Action: do not join in, support, record and report

essays.stem: Describe how you would keep control of your feelings when a customer is rude to you.
essays.modelAnswer: I would remind myself that the customer is upset about the problem and not about me personally. I would take a slow breath and keep my voice low and calm, and my body language open, without folding my arms. I would let the customer speak and listen to what is really wrong, without arguing or answering rudely. I would say that I understand they are upset and tell them what I can do to help. If the customer keeps being rude or becomes threatening, I would politely say that I will get my supervisor, and step away. After the customer leaves, I would take a short break if I need it, talk to someone I trust, and then get back to work. I would also report the incident to my supervisor.
markingPoints: Does not take it personally; stays calm (breathing, calm voice)
Listens without arguing or answering rudely
Shows understanding and offers help
Gets a supervisor if it continues or becomes threatening
Takes a short break or talks to someone and reports the incident

essays.stem: Explain how to give feedback to a co-worker, and how to receive feedback, in a way that keeps good working relationships.
essays.modelAnswer: When giving feedback, choose a private place and a good time, not in front of customers. Talk about the work, not the person. Be specific, for example "The edges on this cut are rough" rather than "Your work is bad". Start with something that was done well, then explain the problem and suggest how to improve. Keep a calm, friendly tone and let the co-worker reply. When receiving feedback, listen without getting angry or making excuses. Ask questions if something is not clear, and thank the person for their help. Think about what was said and use it to improve. If you think the feedback is wrong, explain your view politely at a calm time. Handled this way, feedback builds trust and helps everyone improve.
markingPoints: Give feedback in private, at a good time
Be specific and talk about the work, not the person
Include what was done well and how to improve
Receive feedback calmly, ask questions and say thank you
Use it to improve; disagree politely if needed

essays.stem: Describe how you would help a new trainee settle in during their first week at your workplace.
essays.modelAnswer: On the first day I would greet the trainee, introduce myself and introduce them to the other workers and the supervisor. I would show them around: where to sign in, the toilets, the lunch area, the first-aid kit, the fire exits and the fire extinguishers. I would explain the main rules, such as PPE, keeping the area clean and how to report a problem. I would show them where tools and materials are kept and how to put them away. I would let them watch a task, then try it with me nearby. I would be patient, answer questions kindly and never laugh at mistakes. I would include them at break time so they do not feel alone. At the end of the week I would ask how they are getting on and pass any concerns to the supervisor.
markingPoints: Greets and introduces them to others
Shows the layout: sign-in, facilities, first aid, exits
Explains main rules and safety
Shows how tasks are done, patiently, and answers questions
Includes them socially and checks how they are getting on

essays.stem: Explain what workplace bullying and harassment are, give examples of each, and describe how they should be reported.
essays.modelAnswer: Bullying is repeated behaviour meant to hurt, frighten or embarrass a person. Examples are name-calling, mocking someone's work in front of others, leaving a person out on purpose, hiding their tools, or threatening them. Harassment is unwanted behaviour that offends or upsets a person, often linked to their sex, race, religion or disability. Examples are unwanted touching, sexual comments or jokes, rude messages, or remarks about how someone looks. Both are wrong, damage health and morale, and are against the rules of a good workplace. A person who is bullied or harassed should keep a record of what happened, when and where, and who saw it. They should report it to their supervisor or, if the supervisor is involved, to a manager. Others who see it should support the person and report it too.
markingPoints: Defines bullying (repeated behaviour to hurt or frighten)
Defines harassment (unwanted, offensive behaviour)
Gives suitable examples of each
Keep a record: what, when, where, witnesses
Report to a supervisor or a manager; others should support and report

essays.stem: Describe how a worker can build a good long-term relationship with regular customers.
essays.modelAnswer: A worker builds good relations with regular customers by giving good service every time. They greet the customer by name with a smile, and remember what the customer likes, for example how a client likes her nails done or what size of grill a householder ordered last time. They listen carefully to what the customer wants and explain clearly what can be done, the price and the time it will take. They keep promises: if a job is due on Friday, it is ready on Friday, and if there is a delay they phone the customer early. They are honest about problems and fix mistakes quickly. They stay polite and professional, keep the customer's information private, and thank the customer for coming back. Customers who trust a worker return and recommend the business to others.
markingPoints: Friendly greeting, uses the customer's name, remembers preferences
Listens and explains price and time clearly
Keeps promises and warns early of delays
Honest; fixes mistakes; keeps information private
Says this brings repeat business and recommendations

essays.stem: Compare passive, aggressive and assertive behaviour, and explain why assertive behaviour is best at work.
essays.modelAnswer: A passive person does not say what they think or need. They keep quiet, give in to others to avoid trouble, and may feel used or resentful. For example, they always do the cleaning because they will not ask others to share it. An aggressive person gets their way by shouting, threatening or putting others down. They do not respect other people's views, and others become afraid or angry. An assertive person says clearly and calmly what they think, feel or need, while listening to and respecting others. For example: "I have cleaned the area three days in a row. Can we make a rota so that we share it?" Assertive behaviour is best at work because problems are dealt with openly and fairly, people keep their respect for each other, and the team can agree solutions without fear or bad feeling.
markingPoints: Describes passive behaviour (gives in, does not speak up)
Describes aggressive behaviour (shouts, threatens, ignores others' views)
Describes assertive behaviour (clear, calm, respects others)
Gives an example of assertive behaviour
Explains why assertive is best: fair, open, respectful

practical1.title: Role play: settling a disagreement between co-workers
practical1.brief: As a group, act out and settle a workplace disagreement, then write down the agreement. The assessor gives the group a scenario card, for example two co-workers who keep arguing over a shared grinder and who should clean the bench, or two stylists who disagree about sharing a station and the clean-up. Run the role play at least twice so that every member has a speaking part: two members play the co-workers, one plays the supervisor who helps them talk it through, and the rest observe and note good and poor human relations skills on an observation sheet. In each run the co-workers must explain their side, listen to the other side and agree a fair solution. Then the whole group writes a short agreement sheet: the problem, what each person agreed to do, and when it will be checked. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Observation sheets, one for each observer in each run
Agreement sheet (a blank form or lined paper)
Two chairs and a table for the role play
photos: The group reading the scenario card and agreeing the roles
Each run of the role play, showing the members in their roles
The written agreement sheet for each run, clear enough to read
The group reviewing the role play together at the end
checklist: Stayed calm and used a polite tone and open body language
Listened to the other side without interrupting
Explained their own view clearly without blaming (used "I" statements)
Helped look for a fair solution or compromise
As supervisor, kept the talk fair and let each person speak
As observer, noted at least two good and one poor behaviour accurately
Took part in writing the agreement sheet
safety: Role plays must stay calm: no shouting, pushing or touching
Keep the role play area clear of bags and cables
Use made-up names, not real co-workers or customers

practical2.title: Role play: serving customers with different needs
practical2.brief: As a group, set up a simple reception desk and act out serving customers with different needs. The assessor gives each member a customer card, for example an older person who is hard of hearing, a wheelchair user, a visitor with little English, an impatient customer in a hurry, or a regular customer who wants the same service as last time. The service can be for a welding job, a salon or spa booking, or another trade. Each member serves one customer while another member plays the customer, so every member serves once and plays a customer once. The server greets the customer, finds out what they need, shows respect for their needs, and records the request on a customer service record sheet. The rest of the group observe and note what went well. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Customer service record sheets, one per member
A table and chairs set up as a reception desk, with a clear path for a wheelchair
photos: The reception desk set up, with a clear path to it
Each member greeting their customer (one photo per member)
Each completed customer service record sheet
The group discussing what went well at the end
checklist: Greeted the customer politely, with a smile and eye contact
Spoke to the customer directly, at a suitable pace and with plain words
Showed respect for the customer's needs and background
Found out what the customer needed by asking and listening
Recorded the customer's request correctly on the service record
Stayed patient and calm, including with the impatient customer
Gave fair feedback to another member as an observer
safety: Keep a clear path to the desk and to the exit, with no trailing cables
Do not push a wheelchair or touch a person playing a customer without asking
Keep any real personal details private; use made-up names and numbers
